request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Use fold-level evidence to decide: a config that wins a majority of folds is more trustworthy than one with a higher mean but inconsistent fold performance. Between two configs with similar fold-win rates, prefer the simpler model. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 1 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means one config clearly wins most folds and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means fold wins are split roughly evenly or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run. Compare fold-by-fold: count how many folds each config wins to assess which is genuinely better vs lucky. (Independent run 2.)

concerns: Run 4 wins only 3 of 5 folds (F2, F3, F5). Run 5 wins F1 and run 3 wins F4. Run 4 beats run 1 head-to-head 3-2, and run 1 loses F1 to run 4 by only 0.0005. The mean gap of about 0.004 is far below the fold SD of about 0.06, so run 4 and run 1 are effectively tied.
Run 4 is a little more complex than run 1 because it adds agent features. The gain over run 1 is within noise, so the agent features are not clearly justified.
Fold PR-AUC varies a lot, from about 0.60 to 0.81 across folds. Fold 3 is weak for every config. This points to temporal or cohort instability, and the ~0.73 mean will probably not transfer cleanly.

The PR-AUC of about 0.73 against a 9.35% base rate and the ROC-AUC of about 0.94 look strong for a label of unknown origin. If PotentialFraud was derived from claim patterns, features such as volume or size may leak the label definition. The model may be reproducing the labelling rule, not detecting fraud.
The agent features are only weakly supported. Run 3 (agent plus class weights) is slightly worse than runs 1 and 4, so there is no consistent evidence that agent features or class weighting help.

Precision@50 is about 0.78 and no precision@100 is reported, even though the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Because the labels are only suspicion, this is precision against suspicion and not a confirmed fraud hit rate.

The random forest (run 2) loses every fold to the LightGBM runs, so tree ensembles with class weights do not help. The no_size feature set is consistently worse than all features (run 5 vs run 1), so size features carry signal. That signal is possibly the leakage noted above.

next_experiments.rationale: A simple, regularized baseline. If it gets close to LightGBM's PR-AUC, the simpler model should be preferred. A small gap would also suggest the signal is easy to find, which raises the leakage question.

A more regularized variant of run 4 with fewer leaves and larger leaves' minimum sample size. It tests whether lower variance improves the weak folds (especially F3) without class weighting, which did not help in run 3.
